first_principles_point: Digital control is the business of deciding what online activity is allowed to happen. The internet made action cheap, so trust, identity, permission, routing, security, workflow, and governance became expensive.
money_path: digital activity -> control point -> subscription, usage, bookings, billings, service revenue, or transaction revenue -> renewal and collection -> cost-to-serve -> operating cash and free cash flow
company_examples: Cloudflare; Akamai; Zscaler; Fortinet; Roblox; Okta; CrowdStrike; PayPal; Shopify; Microsoft; ServiceNow
proof_needed: retention; current RPO; deferred revenue; product margin; infrastructure cost; capex; stock compensation; renewal; safety cost; FCF
safe_use: Use as the core no-background framing for digital control, not as proof that every digital metric converts to cash.

first_principles_point: Start with a login. Before work, payment, play, upload, code, or AI action can happen, the system must decide whether the actor is real, safe, permitted, and properly routed.
money_path: user/device/bot/API/agent request -> identity and permission check -> allow/block/route/log decision -> value event -> billed service or transaction -> cash
company_examples: Zscaler; Cloudflare; Fortinet; Akamai; Roblox; Okta; Microsoft
proof_needed: identity checks; policy enforcement; transaction approval; uptime; fraud/security outcomes; cash conversion
safe_use: Use to explain why ordinary online actions depend on hidden control systems.

first_principles_point: Security is permission infrastructure. It decides who, what, and which machine action can access data, applications, networks, payments, and workflows.
money_path: distributed users/devices/data/apps/AI -> security policy/enforcement -> subscription/service/billings -> renewal and expansion -> cash if retention and cost hold
company_examples: Zscaler; Fortinet; Cloudflare; Akamai; CrowdStrike; Palo Alto Networks; Okta; CyberArk; Cisco; Microsoft
proof_needed: gross retention; net retention; renewal rates; product attachment; security outcomes; margin; FCF
safe_use: Use to frame security as operating infrastructure, not only breach response.

first_principles_point: Routing is a product because digital experience fails if traffic is slow, unsafe, unavailable, expensive, or misdirected.
money_path: website/app/API/media/game/AI traffic -> edge network and routing/security layer -> contract or usage revenue -> bandwidth/compute/capex test -> FCF
company_examples: Cloudflare; Akamai; Fastly; F5; Cisco; Arista; DigitalOcean; data-center and connectivity names
proof_needed: traffic quality; bandwidth cost; utilization; capex split; customer concentration; gross margin; FCF
safe_use: Use to show that digital traffic needs route control before it becomes durable economics.

first_principles_point: Identity turns online activity into accountable activity. Without identity, billing, fraud control, permissions, compliance, and platform governance break.
money_path: unknown actor -> identity check -> permission/payment/content/workflow decision -> account-level economics -> collection and retention
company_examples: Okta; Microsoft; Zscaler; Cloudflare; PayPal; Visa; Mastercard; American Express; Shopify; Roblox
proof_needed: fraud losses; account quality; credential durability; customer churn; policy outcomes; payment conversion
safe_use: Use to connect identity to trust, not to claim every identity platform has durable pricing power.

first_principles_point: AI multiplies the control problem. Machine agents can act, route, buy, write, decide, and call APIs, so they need authorization, audit, security, and cost control.
money_path: AI agent/workflow -> policy, identity, data, runtime, route, and security control -> usage/subscription revenue -> infrastructure and support cost -> cash
company_examples: Cloudflare; Zscaler; Akamai; Fortinet; Microsoft; ServiceNow; Salesforce; Shopify; American Express; NVIDIA; Oracle
proof_needed: AI product attachment; AI traffic monetization; usage margin; model/runtime cost; audit and safety evidence
safe_use: Use to say AI raises control demand, not that AI mentions prove monetization.

first_principles_point: Digital growth is only high quality if serving the growth is economical. Traffic, AI, security, gaming, and cloud demand all carry infrastructure, support, bandwidth, capex, and safety costs.
money_path: usage growth -> compute/bandwidth/support/safety/capex burden -> gross margin and OCF -> FCF if cost-to-serve is controlled
company_examples: Cloudflare; Akamai; Zscaler; Fortinet; Roblox; DigitalOcean; Fastly; hyperscalers; data-center operators
proof_needed: cost-to-serve; infrastructure spend; capex; gross margin; support cost; stock compensation; FCF bridge
safe_use: Use as the main boundary against treating digital growth as automatically asset-light.

first_principles_point: Cloudflare shows the protected internet edge: traffic performance, application security, developer runtime, Zero Trust, and machine-traffic governance in one route.
money_path: enterprise/developer/application/security/AI traffic need -> Cloudflare edge/security/runtime contract -> revenue and RPO -> OCF -> FCF if infrastructure, capex, retention, and product attachment hold
proof_needed: dollar-based net retention; current RPO dollars; deferred revenue; Workers/AI Gateway attachment; infrastructure cost; stock compensation; capex; FCF bridge
safe_use: Use as a source-visible protected-edge case with cash-quality boundaries.

first_principles_point: Akamai shows the legacy edge transition: a mature delivery network trying to shift more value into security and distributed cloud infrastructure.
money_path: legacy delivery customer base -> security, compute, and CIS contracts -> revenue and operating cash -> FCF if delivery decline, capex, utilization, and deployment economics hold
proof_needed: delivery decline; security growth; CIS backlog; contract ramp; capex split; segment margin; customer concentration; FCF bridge
safe_use: Use as a transition case, not as proof that legacy delivery drag is solved.

first_principles_point: Zscaler shows access policy as digital control: users, devices, workloads, apps, data, and AI agents need permission before work can happen.
money_path: distributed users/devices/workloads/apps/data/agents -> Zero Trust policy subscription -> ARR/RPO/deferred revenue -> OCF -> FCF if retention, hosting cost, integration, and competition hold
proof_needed: gross retention; net retention; billings; current RPO; deferred revenue aging; product ARR; GAAP loss bridge; stock compensation; hosting cost; FCF
safe_use: Use as source-visible access-policy evidence with retention and cash boundaries.

first_principles_point: Fortinet shows that some digital control remains hardware-attached. Firewalls, branches, carriers, factories, OT environments, and local networks still need physical enforcement plus recurring services.
money_path: hardware/security deployment -> service subscription/support/SASE/OT/FortiGuard -> billings/deferred revenue -> revenue and cash if renewals, channel, product cycle, and attachment hold
proof_needed: renewal rates; billings split; deferred revenue roll-forward; distributor concentration; channel inventory; product/service margin; service attachment; FCF
safe_use: Use as hardware-plus-service control evidence, not as pure SaaS economics.

first_principles_point: Roblox shows governed digital participation. A virtual world has identity, users, creators, payments, discovery, moderation, safety, communication, and virtual currency.
money_path: user attention and creator activity -> Robux purchase/bookings -> deferred and recognized revenue -> creator payouts, safety, moderation, payment fees, infrastructure, and development cost -> cash
proof_needed: Robux recognition; deferred revenue roll-forward; cohort bookings; average bookings per DAU; monetization per hour; creator payout ratio; safety/moderation cost; FCF
safe_use: Use to show platform governance as digital control, not to claim engagement equals durable cash.

first_principles_point: Trust becomes a market when customers cannot personally verify users, devices, transactions, bots, routes, model outputs, merchants, creators, or workloads.
money_path: uncertainty about digital activity -> trust/control vendor -> policy, security, identity, route, audit, or moderation decision -> customer pays -> renewal if trust holds
company_examples: Cloudflare; Akamai; Zscaler; Fortinet; Roblox; Okta; CrowdStrike; PayPal; Visa; Mastercard; American Express; Shopify
proof_needed: trust outcomes; fraud/security metrics; renewal; retention; churn; margin; customer evidence
safe_use: Use to describe trust as a paid product with outcome-proof gaps.

first_principles_point: Memberships, logins, subscriptions, credentials, wallets, paid tiers, and virtual currencies are control systems because they decide who gets access, at what price, and under which rules.
money_path: anonymous/one-time user -> account, membership, credential, subscription, or wallet -> repeated controlled activity -> recurring revenue, fees, data, or bookings -> cash if retention and unit economics hold
company_examples: Roblox; Amazon; American Express; Shopify; PayPal; Netflix; Uber; DoorDash; Microsoft; Adobe
proof_needed: renewal; churn; cohort value; transaction frequency; benefit cost; payment fees; deferred revenue; cash conversion
safe_use: Use to connect platform gates to control without overclaiming customer lifetime value.

first_principles_point: The proof ladder runs from activity visibility to control-point visibility, demand visibility, operating conversion, and durable-control proof. The social question is who sets the rules of digital life.
money_path: digital rule-setting point -> demand metric -> operating conversion -> durable renewal/cash proof -> social power and economic return
company_examples: Cloudflare; Akamai; Zscaler; Fortinet; Roblox; Microsoft; ServiceNow; Shopify; payments and identity platforms
proof_needed: cohort retention; product-level margin; workload profitability; customer-level cash; safety cost; renewal economics; accountability evidence
safe_use: Use to separate theme writing from final durable-control proof.
